topic: Single-sex schools are good for education
pro: No opposite-sex distraction; attainment rises in single-sex cohorts.
Girls take up physics and sport in far greater numbers without male-dominated dynamics.

topic: Society should abolish standardized tests for university admission
pro: Scores track coaching budgets more than ability, laundering privilege as merit.
Test drill crowds out real learning and narrows the curriculum.

topic: Society should teach creationism in schools
pro: Pupils already believe it; ignoring home belief disengages them from science.
Teaching the controversy builds real scientific literacy about evidence.

topic: Society should raise the school leaving age to 18
pro: Credentialled labour markets need it; lifetime earnings rise.
Structured hours cut youth unemployment and idle crime.

topic: Society should introduce year-round schooling
pro: Long summers cause learning loss, worst among the poorest.
Frequent short breaks refresh pupils and staff, cutting burnout.

topic: Society should make sex education mandatory in schools
pro: Universal provision lowers teen pregnancy and STI rates.
Parents alone normalise misinformation, especially in homophobic homes.

topic: Society should support home schooling
pro: Small-group instruction outpaces a class of thirty.
Removes bullying and rigid pacing; networks supply social contact.

topic: Society should allow biased versions of history to be taught
pro: No curriculum is neutral; own the perspective instead of faking objectivity.
A declared bias is teachable - pupils learn to interrogate it.

topic: Society should encourage fewer people to go to university
pro: Credential inflation means degrees no longer signal ability.
Vocational routes are starved while three-year degrees absorb the unneeded.

topic: Society should ban homework
pro: Homework mainly reproduces home advantage and eats family time.
Classroom hours already exceed what other countries use productively.

topic: Society should ban junk food from schools
pro: Schools should model the diet they teach; vending machines contradict lessons.
Childhood obesity costs more than the lost catering revenue.

topic: Society should abolish private schools
pro: Fee-paying schools buy advantage that compounds into elite capture.
Abolition forces one shared system and one shared political constituency.

topic: Society should make school uniforms compulsory
pro: Uniforms mask income gaps and cut morning cost pressure.
They reduce gang colours, branding and exclusion.

topic: Society should make financial literacy a compulsory subject
pro: Debt and pension illiteracy are universal; the state already pays for both.
It is the one subject every pupil will use monthly for life.

topic: Society should abolish grades in primary school
pro: Marks rank children before they can interpret ranking.
Feedback on work beats a number that invites comparison.

topic: Society should make philosophy compulsory for children
pro: Reasoning about argument and ethics transfers to every subject.
Children ask metaphysical questions anyway; give them tools.

topic: Society should ban mobile phones in schools
pro: Phones fragment attention; test scores rise after bans.
They are the main vector for cyberbullying during the day.

topic: Society should abolish university tuition fees
pro: Fees deter poor applicants and load debt onto graduates.
The graduate premium is a public asset, so the public should pay.

topic: Society should make university free for all
pro: Free access maximises talent drawn into research and skills.
Debt aversion shapes career choice away from low-paid public work.

topic: Society should teach coding from primary school
pro: Computational thinking is a basic literacy of the modern economy.
Early exposure closes the gender gap before stereotypes set.

topic: Society should abolish religious education in state schools
pro: Confessional RE teaches unverifiable claims as fact.
Time is better spent on subjects with labour-market and civic payoff.

topic: Society should make a foreign language compulsory to 16
pro: Languages are hard to acquire later; school is the only guaranteed window.
Monolingualism is an economic handicap in a trading economy.

topic: Society should abolish exams at 16
pro: Two-year exam courses truncate breadth at the worst age.
The qualification is no longer used by employers or universities.

topic: Society should replace exams with continuous assessment
pro: One bad morning should not decide a life.
Coursework rewards sustained work rather than memorisation.

topic: Society should introduce a four-day school week
pro: Same contact hours in longer days; fewer commutes and less cost.
A protected day allows tutoring, clinic visits and teacher planning.

topic: Society should pay students for good grades
pro: Cash is a proven motivator for attendance among disengaged pupils.
It mimics the wage incentive school is meant to prepare them for.

topic: Society should abolish school league tables
pro: Tables measure intake, not teaching; poor schools are punished for poverty.
They drive teaching to the test and gaming of entry criteria.

topic: Society should give pupils a vote on school rules
pro: Compliance rises when rules are owned rather than imposed.
It teaches citizenship by practice, not by lecture.

topic: Society should teach debating in every school
pro: Speaking and rebuttal are core employable skills currently left to the lucky.
Debate trains evidence handling better than essay-writing alone.

topic: Society should make music education compulsory
pro: Music improves memory, coordination and group discipline.
It is the only art with no exam-driven protection left.

topic: Society should abolish subject specialisation at 14
pro: Specialising at 14 forecloses options on minimal information.
Breadth protects against a collapsing single industry.

topic: Society should fund boarding places for disadvantaged children
pro: Stability of residence beats chaotic home environments.
Boarding schools hold networks and expectations poor families lack.

topic: Society should ban ability streaming
pro: Streams correlate with class and harden into self-fulfilling labels.
Mixed classes lift the bottom without hurting the top much.

topic: Society should allocate university places by lottery
pro: Above a threshold, differences in score are noise.
A lottery removes the coaching arms race entirely.

topic: Society should abolish the undergraduate dissertation
pro: A single long essay teaches little that coursework does not.
Supervision capacity is stretched thin and quality varies wildly.

topic: Society should teach entrepreneurship in schools
pro: Most pupils will work in small firms or self-employment.
It makes maths and literacy concrete and purposive.

topic: Society should require community service to graduate
pro: Schools exist to make citizens, not only examinees.
Service exposes pupils to lives outside their own postcode.

topic: Society should make PE compulsory to 18
pro: Activity habits set in adolescence persist for life.
Sedentary study is bad for both mood and cognition.

topic: Society should ban competitive sport in primary schools
pro: Losing at seven teaches children to quit sport early.
Cooperation matters more than ranking at that age.

topic: Society should abolish the long summer holiday
pro: Ten weeks is an artefact of the harvest, not modern life.
It is the largest single source of learning loss.

topic: Society should introduce a national curriculum
pro: A common core guarantees portability between schools and regions.
It stops uneven local capacity producing uneven content.

topic: Society should let pupils choose all subjects at 14
pro: Motivation collapses when children study what they resent.
Choice forces schools to justify teaching quality.

topic: Society should make Shakespeare compulsory
pro: Shared cultural reference underpins public argument.
The language work is unmatched preparation for complex text.

topic: Society should teach Latin in state schools
pro: It is the most efficient grammar and vocabulary training available.
It closes a marker of private-school advantage.

topic: Society should abolish academic selection at 11
pro: An 11-plus verdict tracks tutoring and is near-final.
Selection strips comprehensive schools of their strongest intake.

topic: Society should give tutoring vouchers to poor pupils
pro: Tutoring is the biggest driver of attainment gap; vouchers equalise it.
It targets money at the gap rather than at buildings.

topic: Society should stop teachers marking homework
pro: Marking load drives teachers out of the profession.
Self-marking in class gives faster feedback anyway.

topic: Society should make school start at 9am
pro: Adolescent circadian rhythms are genuinely shifted later.
Sleep deprivation is a measurable attainment and mental health cost.

topic: Society should make climate change a compulsory subject
pro: It is the defining policy problem pupils will inherit.
Cross-curricular treatment is patchy and often absent.

topic: Society should abolish lectures
pro: Passive attendance produces worse retention than active seminars.
Recorded content is cheaper and rewatchable.

topic: Society should replace textbooks with tablets
pro: One device carries a whole curriculum and updates free.
Textbook replacement costs exceed device costs within three years.

topic: Society should ignore university rankings
pro: Rankings reward research volume and prestige, not teaching.
They push institutions into gaming and superficial metrics.

topic: Society should publish all student evaluations
pro: Students deserve the information alumni had to guess at.
Publication pressures poor teaching to improve.

topic: Society should pay teachers by performance
pro: Flat pay scales reward tenure over results.
It attracts high performers who currently leave for other sectors.

topic: Society should abolish teacher tenure
pro: Protected jobs resist necessary improvement for decades.
Dismissal should reflect current performance, not 1990s performance.

topic: Society should require teachers to re-certify every five years
pro: Subject knowledge decays; other licensed professions already do this.
It standardises safeguarding and pedagogy updates.

topic: Society should make school meals free for all
pro: Universal provision removes stigma and administrative cost.
Hungry children cannot learn; means-tested schemes miss the borderline poor.

topic: Society should allow phones in school for learning only
pro: Devices are genuinely useful research and accessibility tools.
Bans push use underground rather than teaching management.

topic: Society should teach sign language in all schools
pro: Deaf pupils stop being isolated in mainstream classes.
It is a cheap second language with immediate local use.

topic: Society should make attendance voluntary after 14
pro: Forced attendance of the unwilling poisons classes for everyone.
Fourteen-year-olds can reasonably judge what they want to learn.

topic: Society should ban parental fundraising in schools
pro: PTA fundraising produces wild inequality between neighbouring schools.
It converts parental wealth into school resourcing.

topic: Society should fund teacher training year-round
pro: Current training capacity cannot meet shortage or reform.
Continuous intake smooths the supply pipeline.

topic: Society should teach tax filing in schools
pro: Every adult must do it and most are taught nothing.
It makes numeracy purposeful and reduces exploitation.

topic: Society should require a gap year before university
pro: Maturity improves course choice and reduces dropout.
A year of work or travel broadens the pool of experience.

topic: Society should make internships compulsory for degrees
pro: Work exposure converts study into employability.
It reveals early whether the field suits the student.

topic: Society should ban unpaid internships
pro: Unpaid work excludes everyone who cannot afford it.
Employers extract real value and should pay for it.

topic: Society should cap university class sizes
pro: Seminar learning collapses beyond about twenty students.
Large lectures hide weak teaching and reduce feedback.

topic: Society should replace degree classifications with pass/fail
pro: The two-mark difference between a 2:1 and a 2:2 is statistical noise.
Pass/fail reduces grade inflation pressure on institutions.

topic: Society should abolish the PhD as the entry route to academia
pro: It trains for a job market that cannot absorb the output.
It delays and precarifies careers for years.

topic: Society should give students a statutory right to appeal grades
pro: Assessment errors are common and currently near-unreviewable.
A right of appeal disciplines marker consistency.

topic: Society should make vaccination compulsory
pro: Herd immunity is a public good individuals under-supply.
The unvaccinable are protected by everyone else's compliance.

topic: Society should legalise the sale of human organs
pro: Pricing supply into existence shortens waiting lists that kill.
Regulation ends the exploitation of the existing black market.

topic: Society should introduce universal healthcare
pro: Pooled risk is cheaper and produces better outcomes.
Coverage prevents medical bankruptcy and late-stage emergency care.

topic: Society should deny smokers access to state healthcare
pro: Smokers consume scarce beds and organs others did not waste.
A cost at the point of care is a sharper quit signal than warnings.

topic: Society should introduce minimum alcohol pricing
pro: It targets the cheap high-strength drink driving harmful consumption.
It ends supermarket loss-leader price wars.

topic: The right to die
pro: Autonomy over the body should not stop at the point of suffering.
Refusing treatment already kills; assisted dying just makes it dignified.

topic: Society should ban smoking in cars with children
pro: Concentration in a small cabin far exceeds a smoky room.
Children cannot leave or object.

topic: Society should ban e-cigarettes
pro: Unknown long-term effects, and youth uptake is real.
Vaping renormalises the hand-to-mouth habit and nicotine dependence.

topic: Society should introduce a sugar tax
pro: Price elasticity works; consumption falls measurably.
It pushes reformulation without banning anything.

topic: Society should ban trans fats
pro: They have no nutritional function and cheap substitutes exist.
Denmark eliminated them with no consumer cost.

topic: Society should ban junk food advertising to children
pro: Children cannot distinguish advertising from information.
It removes the pester-power driver of household diet.

topic: Society should require calorie labels on menus
pro: People systematically underestimate portion energy.
It pushes restaurants to reformulate.

topic: Society should legalise cannabis for medical use
pro: Patients with chronic pain and epilepsy report relief conventional drugs fail.
Opioid dependence falls where it is available.

topic: Society should support the legalisation of drugs
pro: Prohibition leaves supply intact while raising price and cutting purity.
Legalisation moves revenue from cartels to treasuries.

topic: Society should decriminalise drug possession
pro: Punishment does not reduce use; treatment does.
Criminal records cost users jobs long after the drug is gone.

topic: Society should fund safe injection sites
pro: Supervised use prevents fatal overdose and infection.
They draw users into contact with services they otherwise avoid.

topic: Society should provide free contraception for all
pro: Unplanned pregnancy costs far more than the pill.
Cost is the main barrier for the young and poor.

topic: Society should restrict breast-milk substitute advertising
pro: Marketing displaces breastfeeding in exactly the countries where it matters.
Formula claims outrun the evidence for them.

topic: Society should protect breastfeeding in public by law
pro: Prosecutions and dirty looks still deter feeding outside.
A right removes the argument entirely.

topic: Society should introduce mental health screening in schools
pro: Half of lifetime conditions emerge before 15 and go unseen.
Schools are the only universal contact point.

topic: Society should legalise commercial surrogacy
pro: Payment widens the pool of surrogates and cuts waits.
It compensates real risk, time and medical burden.

topic: Society should legalise assisted dying for the terminally ill
pro: Safeguards and diagnosis make terminal cases the easiest category.
It ends the worst deaths for those who want control.

topic: Society should adopt opt-out organ donation
pro: Defaults dominate behaviour; donation rates jump.
It costs nothing and preserves the right to refuse.

topic: Society should presume consent for organ donation
pro: Most people support donation but never register.
Presumed consent converts latent support into organs.

topic: Society should abolish private healthcare
pro: Two-tier systems pull staff and capacity away from public patients.
A single payer has the monopsony power to control cost.

topic: Society should abolish prescription charges
pro: Charges deter people from completing courses, causing relapse.
Administration costs rival the revenue.

topic: Society should provide free dental care for all
pro: Dental neglect becomes emergency surgery at several times the cost.
It is the clearest case of prevention paying for itself.

topic: Society should nationalise pharmaceutical research
pro: Public money funds most basic discovery, then firms price the result.
Profit-driven agendas neglect antibiotics and tropical disease.

topic: Society should require drug companies to publish all trial data
pro: Unpublished negative trials distort the entire evidence base.
Regulators already hold the data; secrecy is a choice.

topic: Society should abolish patents on life-saving medicines
pro: Monopoly pricing rations drugs by income, not need.
Generic competition collapses price within months.

topic: Society should allow generic manufacture in health emergencies
pro: Compulsory licensing already exists; make it automatic.
Delay costs lives that patents do not save.

topic: Society should ban direct-to-consumer drug advertising
pro: Patients arrive demanding brands with no better outcomes.
It drives spend on marketing rather than on trial design.

topic: Society should treat severe childhood obesity as a child protection matter
pro: In the worst cases it is a failure of care like neglect.
It triggers statutory support families cannot access otherwise.

topic: Society should tax drinks by sugar content
pro: A sliding scale drives reformulation harder than a flat levy.
It aligns the tax with the actual harm gradient.

topic: Society should ban energy drinks for under-16s
pro: Caffeine doses exceed adult guidance in a child-sized body.
They displace sleep and water in the worst-consumption groups.

topic: Society should fund school breakfast clubs
pro: Hunger is the single most fixable barrier to learning.
They raise attendance and punctuality measurably.

topic: Society should ban vending machines in hospitals
pro: Hospitals should not sell the disease they treat.
They undercut dietary advice at the moment of maximum salience.

topic: Society should legalise medicinal psychedelics
pro: Trial evidence for treatment-resistant depression is strong.
Existing drugs fail a large share of patients entirely.

topic: Society should regulate alternative medicine
pro: Practitioners make medical claims with no evidence standard.
Regulation lets the good modalities separate from the nonsense.

topic: Society should ban insurers excluding pre-existing conditions
pro: Being uninsurable when sick defeats the point of insurance.
It removes the incentive to churn policies before diagnosis.

topic: Society should make health insurance compulsory
pro: Mandates stop the young free-riding and flatten the risk pool.
Universal coverage needs universal contribution.

topic: Society should cap hospital executive pay
pro: Pay spirals regardless of clinical outcomes.
The saving is real capacity at ward level.

topic: Society should publish surgeon success rates
pro: Patients choose on evidence rather than reputation.
Publication drives genuine quality improvement.

topic: Society should let patients choose any hospital
pro: Choice forces poor units to improve or close.
It breaks postcode lotteries in outcome quality.

topic: Society should abolish hospital parking charges
pro: Parking taxes illness, and hits visitors most.
Revenue is small against the access barrier it creates.

topic: Society should pay blood donors
pro: Payment secures supply against seasonal shortage.
Donation costs time and travel that altruism does not reimburse.

topic: Society should allow paid plasma donation
pro: Plasma is a manufactured product, not a scarce gift.
Payment ends dependence on imports for immune therapies.

topic: Society should cap doctors' shifts at 48 hours
pro: Fatigue degrades judgement in a way that kills patients.
Handover errors cluster at the end of long shifts.

topic: Society should make rest breaks statutory for nurses
pro: Missed breaks are routine and compound error.
A legal floor stops goodwill being exploited.

topic: Society should make midwife-led home birth the default
pro: Home birth is as safe for low-risk pregnancy and far cheaper.
Continuity of carer is the strongest known outcome driver.

topic: Society should restrict caesareans on demand
pro: Unnecessary surgery carries real recovery and infection cost.
Capacity is finite and elective sections crowd out emergencies.

topic: Society should fund doulas under public insurance
pro: Continuous support shortens labour and reduces intervention.
It is the cheapest clinical input available.

topic: Society should fund IVF on public health systems
pro: Infertility is a medical condition, not a luxury.
Cost barriers currently decide who becomes a parent.

topic: Society should cap publicly funded IVF cycles
pro: Uncapped funding crowds out other treatment for the same budget.
Diminishing returns set in after a small number of cycles.

topic: Society should allow sex selection for family balancing
pro: Most families want one of each and it is a marginal cost.
Selection ends the regret of repeated pregnancies.

topic: Society should restrict cosmetic surgery advertising
pro: Ads sell insecurity and hide risk and revision rates.
Prices and outcomes stay opaque to patients.

topic: Society should require health warnings on alcohol labels
pro: Alcohol is the only major carcinogen sold without a label.
Consumers currently cannot know unit content without effort.

topic: Society should ban tobacco sponsorship of sport
pro: Sport reaches exactly the demographics smoking recruits.
It removes the last route to mass brand exposure.

topic: Society should make plain packaging compulsory
pro: Plain packs break the pack as an advert.
It ends the packaging gimmick arms race.

topic: Society should fund telemedicine in rural areas
pro: Distance is the main access barrier and travel costs fall away.
It is cheaper than staffing full remote clinics.

topic: Society should go nuclear
pro: Only dispatchable low-carbon source at the scale climate targets need.
Deaths per unit of power remain far below fossil fuels.

topic: Society should store nuclear waste underground
pro: Deep geology isolates long-lived waste for the necessary timescales.
It unblocks the nuclear programme it currently constrains.

topic: Society should ban single-use plastics
pro: Alternatives exist and the waste stream is the main ocean load.
It removes the item used for minutes and lasts centuries.

topic: Society should introduce a carbon tax
pro: The cheapest abatement is found first by price, not mandate.
Revenue can be recycled as a dividend to protect the poor.

topic: Society should prefer cap-and-trade to a carbon tax
pro: A cap guarantees the emissions outcome the science requires.
Trading allocates abatement to whoever can do it cheapest.

topic: Society should ban petrol and diesel car sales by 2035
pro: A firm end date drives manufacturers to invest now.
The charging network follows the same signal.

topic: Society should subsidise electric vehicles
pro: Early subsidy buys the learning curve that cuts price for everyone.
It protects air quality in the streets where it is worst.

topic: Society should ban short-haul domestic flights
pro: Rail beats air under three hours door to door.
Per-passenger emissions are multiples of the rail alternative.

topic: Society should tax aviation fuel
pro: Aviation is the largest untaxed transport fuel by design.
It is the fastest-growing emissions source in most rich states.

topic: Society should introduce a frequent flyer levy
pro: It targets the small minority who fly most.
It is progressive in a way a flat ticket tax is not.

topic: Society should ban fracking
pro: Methane leakage erodes the climate case.
It locks in gas infrastructure for decades.

topic: Society should divest public funds from fossil fuels
pro: Divestment removes the licence of respectability from the sector.
It exposes the stranded-asset risk pensioners will otherwise eat.

topic: Society should ban new coal plants
pro: Coal is the single largest emissions source and substitutes exist.
Plants built now will run for forty years.

topic: Society should subsidise renewable generation
pro: Subsidy bought the cost collapses we now enjoy.
It shifts risk from pioneer investors to the public who benefit.

topic: Society should introduce feed-in tariffs
pro: They turn millions of rooftops into generation capacity.
Small producers are paid a fair price rather than an exploitative one.

topic: Society should ban new offshore drilling
pro: Spill risk is concentrated and near-permanent.
Offshore gas is the most expensive barrel left.

topic: Society should ban deep-sea mining
pro: Nodule ecosystems recover on timescales no one has measured.
We know the surface; we do not know the seabed.

topic: Society should protect 30% of oceans
pro: Fish stocks rebound measurably in fully protected zones.
It is the floor the science names for functioning ecosystems.

topic: Society should ban bottom trawling
pro: Trawling scrapes the seabed carbon sink along with the catch.
Bycatch ratios are indefensible.

topic: Society should ban commercial whaling
pro: Whales are the ocean's nutrient pump and carbon store.
The economics of hunting have long since collapsed.

topic: Society should ban shark finning
pro: Fins are cut and the animal dumped to die.
Apex removal cascades through the whole food web.

topic: Society should ban trophy hunting
pro: Fees rarely reach the communities near the animals.
It removes the largest individuals from breeding stock.

topic: Society should legalise the ivory trade
pro: Legal supply satisfies demand without poaching pressure.
Bans leave stockpiles to rot and prices high.

topic: Society should ban palm oil
pro: Monoculture plantation replaces the highest-carbon forest.
Labelling lets consumers act immediately.

topic: Society should require carbon labels on products
pro: Consumers cannot price what they cannot see.
It rewards firms that already decarbonised.

topic: Society should mandate emissions disclosure for firms
pro: Investors are pricing blind without it.
Disclosure forces the internal accounting that precedes change.

topic: Society should pay climate reparations
pro: Emitters took the atmospheric space others now cannot use.
Adaptation costs land on those who emitted least.

topic: Society should create a loss and damage fund
pro: It answers irreversible harm, not just future mitigation.
It is the cheapest route to climate diplomacy surviving.

topic: Society should ban geoengineering
pro: Solar management treats a symptom and creates a termination shock risk.
Governance is undefined and unilateral deployment is likely.

topic: Society should fund solar geoengineering research
pro: Research is cheap against the option value.
We may need a fast brake if tipping points arrive early.

topic: Society should ban non-native afforestation
pro: Monocultures of foreign species support little wildlife.
They can release more carbon than they store.

topic: Society should rewild half of farmland
pro: Agriculture occupies the majority of habitable land for a minority of output.
Rewilding restores flood, carbon and species capacity at once.

topic: Society should ban peat extraction
pro: Peat bogs are the densest terrestrial carbon store.
Garden compost has easy substitutes.

topic: Society should tax meat
pro: Beef costs several times the emissions of plant protein.
Price is the only lever that shifts the weekly shop.

topic: Society should ban factory farming
pro: Confinement is the single biggest animal welfare failure.
It concentrates antibiotic use and zoonotic risk.

topic: Society should phase out subsidies to animal agriculture
pro: Public money currently buys the most polluting protein.
It frees budget to make plant and novel protein competitive.

topic: Society should promote lab-grown meat
pro: It removes land, water and slaughter from the equation.
Public research can replicate the renewables cost curve.

topic: Society should ban live animal exports
pro: Transport stress kills a measurable share in transit.
Exporting carcasses moves less weight and volume.

topic: Society should ban cage farming
pro: Cages remove almost every natural behaviour.
Cage-free production costs consumers only pennies an egg.

topic: Society should require import welfare standards
pro: Domestic farmers otherwise compete against worse practice.
It exports welfare improvement to producer countries.

topic: Society should ban zoos
pro: Enclosures cannot replicate range, migration or social group size.
Conservation claims are mostly captive breeding that rarely releases.

topic: Society should ban aquariums
pro: Large marine animals suffer extreme confinement.
Capture damages wild populations for display.

topic: Society should abolish agricultural subsidies
pro: Subsidies distort planting toward surplus and starve efficient foreign producers.
They capitalise into land price, not farmer income.

topic: Society should end biofuel mandates
pro: Crop fuel competes directly with food for land.
Lifecycle savings are often negligible or negative.

topic: Society should ban supermarket food waste
pro: Edible food dumped while food banks ration is indefensible.
Waste disposal costs more than redistribution.

topic: Society should require supermarkets to sell misshapen produce
pro: Cosmetic standards throw away a third of harvests.
Price it cheaper and consumers buy it.

topic: Society should tax packaging by weight
pro: It puts the disposal cost on the producer who chose the design.
Weight is a simple, ungameable proxy.

topic: Society should make deposit return schemes mandatory
pro: Return rates above 90% are routine where they exist.
It produces clean single-material streams worth recycling.

topic: Society should ban bottled water in public buildings
pro: Tap water is cheaper, tested to a higher standard and needs no plastic.
Public bodies should model the norm.

topic: Society should renationalise water utilities
pro: Private operators prioritise dividends over pipe replacement.
Water is a natural monopoly with no competitive discipline.

topic: Society should ban water privatisation in developing states
pro: Concession contracts have repeatedly raised prices on the poorest.
Conditionality has forced privatisation regardless of local capacity.

topic: Society should require universal water metering
pro: Unmetered households have no feedback on use.
Metering cut consumption sharply wherever introduced.

topic: Society should ban golf courses in dry regions
pro: A single course can drink as much as a small town.
They serve a narrow, wealthy membership.

topic: Society should subsidise desalination
pro: It is drought-proof supply when reservoirs fail.
Renewable-powered plants remove the energy objection.

topic: Society should ban private jets
pro: Per-passenger emissions are ten to twenty times commercial.
They carry a tiny share of travellers for a huge share of the carbon.

topic: Society should tax private jets heavily
pro: A ban is blunt; a tax scales with use.
It captures the corporate flyers who can afford to change.

topic: Society should ban cruise ships from fragile waters
pro: Discharge and anchor damage hit the most sensitive habitats.
Ship numbers are growing fastest in exactly those areas.

topic: Society should mandate electrification of shipping
pro: Short-sea and port movement is already electrifiable.
It removes the dirtiest fuel from the coastlines people live on.

topic: Society should ban heavy fuel oil in the Arctic
pro: A spill there cannot be cleaned in ice.
Black carbon deposits accelerate local melt.

topic: Society should create green shipping corridors
pro: Concentrating fuel infrastructure on a few routes makes it viable.
It gives first movers a route to scale.

topic: Society should subsidise heat pumps
pro: Upfront cost is the only real barrier to a mature technology.
It cuts both bills and emissions immediately.

topic: Society should ban gas boilers in new homes
pro: Retrofitting later costs several times more than building right.
New build is the cheapest possible moment to switch.

topic: Society should mandate home insulation standards
pro: Insulation is the cheapest energy ever produced.
Cold homes kill more people than road accidents.

topic: Society should fund retrofitting grants
pro: Most housing stock predates any efficiency standard.
Grants reach households that cannot borrow.

topic: Society should ban gas cookers in new builds
pro: Combustion indoors worsens asthma in children.
The wiring is already there for induction.

topic: Society should promote community energy ownership
pro: Local ownership keeps the revenue and the consent local.
It defuses the planning opposition that blocks projects.

topic: Society should allow municipal green bonds
pro: Cities can fund retrofit faster than central budgets allow.
Investors get a secure, ring-fenced return.

topic: Society should restrict light pollution
pro: Light spill disrupts insect, bird and bat ecology.
Shielded fittings cost nothing extra.

topic: Society should create dark sky reserves
pro: They protect the last unlit habitats and draw tourism.
They cost a planning designation, not a budget.

topic: Society should restrict private fireworks
pro: Particulate spikes and wildlife panic are measurable.
Public displays deliver more spectacle per unit of pollution.

topic: Society should abolish the minimum wage
pro: It prices out the least productive workers it claims to help.
A wage floor cannot respond to local labour conditions.

topic: Society should raise the minimum wage to a living wage
pro: A full-time job should end in-work poverty.
Subsidy to low-wage employers currently tops up their payroll.

topic: Society should introduce universal basic income
pro: It removes the trap and stigma of means testing.
It is the only transfer that fits fragmented gig work.

topic: Society should introduce a negative income tax
pro: It targets the poor while keeping work incentives intact.
It replaces a maze of overlapping benefits with one taper.

topic: Society should cap the executive pay ratio
pro: Ratios have decoupled from any performance measure.
Boards ratchet each other upward regardless of results.

topic: Society should introduce mandatory salary capping
pro: Capped wage bills let firms cut prices to consumers.
It narrows the gap that corrodes internal morale.

topic: Society should put workers on company boards
pro: Decisions that cut jobs should include the people cut.
It is standard in the economies with the least labour unrest.

topic: Society should mandate profit sharing
pro: It aligns staff with long-term firm success.
It lifts pay without raising fixed costs in downturns.

topic: Society should abolish inheritance tax
pro: It is levied on already-taxed wealth.
It falls on small estates the threshold never catches up with.

topic: Society should raise inheritance tax
pro: Inherited wealth is the main driver of stalled mobility.
It is the least distortionary tax available.

topic: Society should introduce a wealth tax
pro: Assets have grown far faster than income and escape income tax.
The revenue base is concentrated and administrable.

topic: Society should introduce a land value tax
pro: Land cannot be hidden or moved offshore.
It taxes the value the public created, not the owner's effort.

topic: Society should introduce a financial transaction tax
pro: It prices the high-frequency churn that adds little liquidity.
Even a tiny rate raises very large revenue.

topic: Society should introduce a Tobin tax
pro: It dampens destabilising currency speculation.
Revenue can fund development commitments already promised.

topic: Society should abolish corporation tax
pro: It is ultimately paid by workers and customers anyway.
It drives profit-shifting and incorporation games.

topic: Society should introduce a digital services tax
pro: Platforms book revenue in low-tax jurisdictions regardless of users.
It captures value created by user data.

topic: Society should create a global minimum corporate tax
pro: It ends the race to the bottom that starves every treasury.
Coordination is the only defence against profit-shifting.

topic: Society should abolish tax havens
pro: Trillions sit outside the reach of the states that produced them.
Shell registration is the core mechanism and can be closed.

topic: Society should mandate country-by-country reporting
pro: Public scrutiny is what makes transfer pricing honest.
Regulators currently see only what firms volunteer.

topic: Society should abolish cash
pro: Cash is the vehicle for the shadow economy and tax evasion.
Every transaction becomes traceable and cheap to process.

topic: Society should cap cash payments
pro: A cap hits evasion without removing cash entirely.
It is already standard across much of Europe.

topic: Society should abolish tipping
pro: It makes pay unpredictable and dependent on mood.
It exports US-style insecurity into other labour markets.

topic: Society should make service charges mandatory
pro: Menu prices should tell the truth about the cost.
Staff get a stable income rather than a nightly lottery.

topic: Society should introduce a four-day week
pro: Output holds or rises where it has been trialled.
It distributes productivity gains as time rather than only money.

topic: Society should create a right to disconnect
pro: Smartphones made the working day borderless.
Unpaid availability is work and should be bounded.

topic: Society should ban zero-hours contracts
pro: Workers carry all the demand risk with none of the security.
Employers rarely need the flexibility they claim.

topic: Society should make gig benefits portable
pro: Platform workers move between apps and lose everything each time.
Portability preserves flexibility without abandoning security.

topic: Society should classify gig workers as employees
pro: Platforms control pay, rating and dismissal like any employer.
Misclassification shifts cost onto the public purse.

topic: Society should encourage gig economy unionisation
pro: Collective voice is the only counterweight to algorithmic control.
Fragmented workers cannot bargain individually.

topic: Society should abolish collective bargaining rights
pro: Insider unions can price out the unemployed.
Sector-wide deals entrench incumbents against new entrants.

topic: Society should introduce sectoral bargaining
pro: It covers the small firms where union density is lowest.
It stops good employers being undercut by bad ones.

topic: Society should guarantee the right to strike in essential services
pro: Essential work is exactly where bargaining power is weakest.
Minimum-service agreements answer the safety objection.

topic: Society should ban strike-breaking agency staff
pro: Agency cover blunts the strike's only leverage.
It is cheap for employers to arrange at the last minute.

topic: Society should make works councils mandatory
pro: They surface problems before they become disputes.
They cost little and reduce turnover.

topic: Society should abolish non-compete clauses
pro: Most workers never see a trade secret yet cannot move.
They suppress wages by locking people in.

topic: Society should ban unpaid overtime
pro: Unpaid hours are the largest hidden subsidy to employers.
It rewards efficiency over presenteeism.

topic: Society should cap the working week at 40 hours
pro: Long hours stop adding output after a point and start adding error.
A cap forces better work design.

topic: Society should introduce statutory paternity leave
pro: Take-up by fathers shifts the domestic load permanently.
It is the main lever against the motherhood pay penalty.

topic: Society should introduce shared parental leave
pro: It lets families allocate care to whoever earns less.
It removes the assumption that the mother will take it.

topic: Society should treat childcare as public infrastructure
pro: Without it, paid work is impossible for a parent.
Returns in tax revenue exceed the subsidy.

topic: Society should provide free childcare from birth
pro: Cost peaks exactly when parents can least afford it.
Early years provision pays back over a lifetime.

topic: Society should make child benefit universal
pro: Means testing creates cliff edges and administrative cost.
Universality builds the political coalition that protects it.

topic: Society should abolish means testing
pro: Tapers trap people and cost more to administer than they save.
Universal systems are harder to stigmatise and easier to defend.

topic: Society should reform housing benefit
pro: Payment to landlords lets rents chase the subsidy.
Local caps bear no relation to local markets.

topic: Society should introduce rent controls
pro: Rents have outrun wages for two decades.
Security of tenure lets communities stay put.

topic: Society should abolish stamp duty
pro: It taxes mobility and freezes people in wrong-sized homes.
Transaction taxes are the most distortive of all.

topic: Society should capture land value for infrastructure
pro: Public investment creates private windfalls nobody earned.
It funds the next line without general taxation.

topic: Society should require social housing quotas in new developments
pro: New supply should not be exclusively market-rate.
It creates mixed communities instead of segregated ones.

topic: Society should extend the right to buy
pro: Ownership builds a stake and a stake builds stability.
Receipts fund replacement stock.

topic: Society should ban foreign ownership of housing
pro: Absentee capital treats homes as a vault, not a residence.
It removes a demand stream untethered to local wages.

topic: Society should tax empty homes
pro: Vacancy is a pure waste of finished supply.
A tax makes holding out for capital gain expensive.

topic: Society should restrict short-term rentals in cities
pro: Whole flats removed from the long-term market cut local supply.
Hotels pay commercial rates that Airbnb hosts do not.

topic: Society should cap short-term rental density
pro: A cap preserves a residential core in tourist districts.
It stops a single operator buying a whole street.

topic: Society should abolish height restrictions
pro: Cities with the least height limit have the most affordable housing.
Land in the centre is the most valuable and least used.

topic: Society should introduce upzoning by right
pro: Certainty removes the years of negotiation that block building.
Small sites get built where megaprojects stall.

topic: Society should reform the green belt
pro: It is a 1950s line around 2020s cities.
Small releases near stations cost almost no landscape.

topic: Society should abolish mortgage interest relief
pro: It subsidises debt and bids prices up.
It is a subsidy to owners paid by renters.

topic: Society should mandate long fixed-rate mortgages
pro: Rate shocks repossess households that budgeted correctly.
It removes a systemic stability risk.

topic: Society should expand credit unions
pro: Member ownership ends the shareholder extraction.
They serve the borrowers banks reject.

topic: Society should introduce postal banking
pro: The branch network already exists in every community.
It reaches the unbanked where banks withdrew.

topic: Society should cap payday loan interest
pro: Annualised rates reach four figures.
A cap is the only thing that has made them sane.

topic: Society should create a public banking option
pro: A public provider sets a benchmark private banks must beat.
It is the answer to branch deserts.

topic: Society should abolish student debt
pro: Debt suppresses house buying, saving and family formation.
Much of it is interest on maintenance, not tuition.

topic: Society should limit loans to income-contingent terms
pro: Repayment should track ability to pay, not a calendar.
It removes the default risk that ruins young credit files.

topic: Society should create a resource sovereign wealth fund
pro: Extracted assets are finite and belong to future citizens too.
It stops a boom being spent in one political cycle.

topic: Society should pay a citizens' dividend
pro: It returns common asset income to the people who own it.
It is simple, universal and impossible to stigmatise.

topic: Society should abolish farm price floors
pro: Floors create permanent surplus and storage mountains.
They shelter the largest producers, not the smallest.

topic: Society should abolish fuel subsidies
pro: They are the most regressive subsidy in most developing states.
They lock in the most polluting consumption.

topic: Society should introduce a carbon border adjustment
pro: It stops decarbonisation being undercut by imports.
It pushes the standard outward to trading partners.

topic: Society should adopt strategic industrial policy
pro: Markets underinvest in capacity with long lead times and public payoff.
Every serious economy is already doing it.

topic: Society should build sovereign semiconductor capacity
pro: Chip supply is a national security dependency.
Shortages have already halted whole industries.

topic: Society should block foreign takeovers of strategic firms
pro: Technology and know-how migrate with ownership.
Screening is cheap and reversible.

topic: Society should use golden shares in critical industry
pro: It protects public interest without nationalisation.
Investors still get capital markets and management.

topic: Society should reform export credit agencies
pro: They underwrite fossil projects their governments claim to oppose.
The subsidy is invisible in every climate budget.

topic: Society should abolish export subsidies
pro: They favour large exporters who would sell abroad anyway.
They distort both domestic and destination markets.

topic: Society should make fair trade certification mandatory
pro: Voluntary labels are bought by a small conscientious niche.
Mandatory floors lift the whole market at once.

topic: Society should abolish tariffs on green goods
pro: Solar and turbine costs fall for every importer.
Climate goods should not be taxed at borders.

topic: Society should adopt unilateral free trade
pro: Consumers gain immediately without waiting on reciprocity.
It removes the leverage protectionist lobbies use.

topic: Society should abolish consensus voting at the WTO
pro: One member can stall a package for everyone.
Consensus entrenches the least reformist states.

topic: Society should open public procurement data
pro: It exposes overpricing and collusion immediately.
Contractors behave differently when watched.

topic: Society should create public beneficial ownership registers
pro: Shell ownership hides crime, tax and sanctions evasion.
Registration costs almost nothing to administer.

topic: Society should ban shell companies
pro: A firm with no office or staff exists only to obscure.
Substance requirements close the loophole properly.

topic: Society should require pay ratio disclosure
pro: Publicity alone has narrowed gaps where tried.
Employees deserve to know the shape of their firm.

topic: Society should mandate audit firm rotation
pro: Long tenure breeds cosiness with management.
Fresh eyes catch what familiarity misses.

topic: Society should break up the Big Four accountancy firms
pro: They audit, consult and advise the same client.
Four firms is not a competitive market.

topic: Society should remove limited liability for major polluters
pro: Limited liability externalises environmental risk onto the public.
Unlimited exposure forces real insurance and care.

topic: Society should create corporate criminal liability for negligence
pro: Currently only a named individual is ever charged.
Fines on the entity are the only sanction that changes behaviour.

topic: Society should cap executive severance pay
pro: Rewarding failure with millions destroys the incentive story.
Boards negotiate severance against no benchmark.

topic: Society should abolish performance-related pay for executives
pro: It rewards short-term metrics and invites gaming.
Executives are already paid enough to try hard.

topic: Society should make board quotas for women mandatory
pro: Voluntary targets have plateaued well below parity.
Quotas change the shortlist, then the culture.

topic: Society should abolish the US Electoral College
pro: One person, one vote is the basic principle; it lets losers win.
Winner-take-all makes most states spectators.

topic: Society should adopt proportional representation
pro: First-past-the-post hands majorities to minority vote shares.
PR ends wasted votes and lifts turnout.

topic: Society should introduce recall elections
pro: Elections every four years are too blunt for scandal.
Recall disciplines behaviour continuously.

topic: Society should enforce executive term limits
pro: Incumbency advantage stops elections being competitive.
Limits break drift toward personalist rule.

topic: Society should hold referendums on new EU treaties
pro: Treaties transfer sovereignty and need direct mandate.
Elite avoidance bred the anti-EU backlash.

topic: Society should have no elections rather than sham elections
pro: Sham ballots lend regimes unearned legitimacy.
They teach citizens their vote is meaningless.

topic: Society should impose democracy
pro: Democracies fight each other less and protect rights better.
Post-war imposition has worked in Germany, Japan and the Balkans.

topic: Society should abolish Democratic superdelegates
pro: Unelected grandees can outweigh primary voters.
Their weight ends contests before most states vote.

topic: Society should allow internet voting
pro: Turnout rises among young, disabled, rural and overseas voters.
Counts are faster and cheaper.

topic: Society should introduce compulsory voting
pro: Turnout above 90% makes results genuinely representative.
It forces parties to address the apathetic, not just the engaged.

topic: Society should lower the voting age to 16
pro: Sixteen-year-olds pay tax and can work and marry.
Voting habit formed young persists for life.

topic: Society should give 16-year-olds the local vote
pro: Local decisions affect them most and they have least voice.
Local elections are the safest place to learn.

topic: Society should abolish the voting age entirely
pro: Any arbitrary line excludes someone competent.
Parents already act as proxies; the child's interest is real.

topic: Society should introduce open primaries
pro: Closed primaries let a small partisan base pick the candidate.
Open contests reward general-election appeal.

topic: Society should abolish party whips
pro: Whips convert representatives into voting machines.
Free votes produce better-argued legislation.

topic: Society should have free votes on conscience issues
pro: Abortion, euthanasia and war are not party matters.
Constituents elect a person, not a bloc.

topic: Society should elect the upper house
pro: An appointed chamber can veto an elected one without mandate.
Election is the minimum price of legislative power.

topic: Society should abolish the upper house
pro: Second chambers mostly duplicate and delay.
Unicameral states legislate faster with no measurable harm.

topic: Society should abolish the monarchy
pro: Hereditary office is an anomaly in a democracy.
Reserve powers sit with an unaccountable family.

topic: Society should directly elect the head of state
pro: Election confers a mandate the office currently lacks.
It ends the accident of who the family produces.

topic: Society should abolish the cabinet
pro: Cabinet government concentrates power in twenty people.
Full committees scrutinise better than a weekly meeting.

topic: Society should elect judges
pro: Judges make policy and should answer to the public.
Election breaks the closed professional pipeline.

topic: Society should impose judicial term limits
pro: Lifetime tenure can mean forty years on a changing world.
Regular renewal keeps the bench in touch.

topic: Society should create judicial appointments commissions
pro: They break executive patronage of the bench.
Merit criteria beat personal networks.

topic: Society should publish supreme court deliberations
pro: Public reasoning is what legitimates the ruling.
Secrecy hides the actual ratio of the decision.

topic: Society should televise court proceedings
pro: Justice seen is justice trusted.
It educates the public about how law actually works.

topic: Society should abolish jury duty exemptions
pro: Exemptions produce juries skewed to the retired and unbusy.
A duty borne by all is a duty respected.

topic: Society should use citizen assemblies for constitutional change
pro: Random selection beats partisan advantage in design.
Deliberation produces better-informed preferences.

topic: Society should create sortition chambers
pro: Random citizens are immune to donor pressure and re-election.
Deliberation shows ordinary people govern well.

topic: Society should introduce participatory budgeting
pro: Residents know which pavement actually floods.
It builds engagement in the money that is closest to them.

topic: Society should require local referendums on major planning
pro: Development decisions are irreversible and local.
It buys consent that appeals cannot.

topic: Society should devolve power to city regions
pro: Decisions are better made near the affected streets.
It ends the capital's gravitational monopoly.

topic: Society should abolish county councils
pro: Two tiers of local government duplicate and confuse.
Savings can go to frontline services.

topic: Society should introduce metro mayors
pro: One accountable figure beats a committee of leaders.
Transport and skills need a single strategic hand.

topic: Society should abolish hereditary peers
pro: Birth is the only qualification required.
The chamber is already mostly appointed; finish the job.

topic: Society should cap political donations
pro: Large donors buy disproportionate access.
Caps are already standard in comparable democracies.

topic: Society should publicly fund political parties
pro: It reduces dependence on private money.
Public funding can be tied to membership and transparency.

topic: Society should abolish private political donations
pro: Any donation is a claim on future favour.
Public funding alone removes the market entirely.

topic: Society should cap election spending
pro: Costs deter good candidates without networks.
Spending caps shorten the arms race.

topic: Society should mandate transparency in political advertising
pro: Voters cannot judge an ad without knowing who paid.
The current funding trail is deliberately obscure.

topic: Society should regulate campaign micro-targeting
pro: Different voters get contradictory promises invisibly.
The 2016 campaigns showed the scale of the gap.

topic: Society should ban political advertising on social media
pro: Platforms cannot verify claims and have no liability.
Bans force parties back to auditable channels.

topic: Society should mandate fact-check labels on political claims
pro: Misinformation spreads faster than correction.
A label puts the correction in the same frame.

topic: Society should create a right of reply for candidates
pro: A false attack should not outlive the campaign.
It costs the broadcaster a minute of air.

topic: Society should make campaign data public
pro: Voter files built from public data should be auditable.
It lets smaller parties compete.

topic: Society should restrict lobbyist access to parliament
pro: Access currently tracks who can afford a pass.
Restriction forces the register to mean something.

topic: Society should impose a cooling-off period on ministers becoming lobbyists
pro: They arrive knowing the files and the officials.
Two years removes the sharpest insider edge.

topic: Society should publish ministerial diaries
pro: Who a minister meets is who influences them.
Publication is cheap and immediate.

topic: Society should create an independent ethics commission
pro: Self-regulation of conduct has failed repeatedly.
Outside sanction is the only credible deterrent.

topic: Society should let parliament recall ministers
pro: Resignation convention is dying.
A formal mechanism beats waiting for a reshuffle.

topic: Society should abolish the royal prerogative
pro: War and treaty powers bypass parliament entirely.
Codification puts them on a statutory footing.

topic: Society should codify a written constitution
pro: Unwritten rules are whatever the incumbent says they are.
Codification protects minorities from convention drift.

topic: Society should entrench a bill of rights
pro: Entrenchment stops transient majorities eroding rights.
Courts need a text to enforce.

topic: Society should reform permanent UNSC seats
pro: The 1945 map no longer matches the world.
Reform restores the Council's credibility.

topic: Society should abolish federal second chambers
pro: They duplicate and slow without improving output.
State interests are already represented elsewhere.

topic: Society should adopt unicameralism
pro: Two chambers create gridlock and hide accountability.
Nebraska works with one.

topic: Society should abolish state governors
pro: They duplicate the federal executive at state cost.
One chain of accountability is clearer.

topic: Society should cap legislature size
pro: Chambers of 700 are unmanageable and expensive.
Smaller chambers vote better on the same bills.

topic: Society should allow citizen-initiated referendums
pro: It is the check when parliament refuses to act.
Signature thresholds stop frivolous use.

topic: Society should abolish the filibuster
pro: A 60-vote supermajority exists nowhere in the constitution.
It lets 41 senators block anything at no cost.

topic: Society should abolish the debt ceiling
pro: It is a second vote on spending already agreed.
Every fight is a manufactured default risk.

topic: Society should adopt a balanced budget amendment
pro: Deficits are easy now and painful later.
It forces trade-offs to be explicit.

topic: Society should give the executive a line-item veto
pro: It strips pork attached to must-pass bills.
It reduces total spend without cutting programmes.

topic: Society should adopt the single transferable vote
pro: Ranked ballots let voters back small parties without wasting the vote.
Multi-member districts make results proportional.

topic: Society should use open party lists
pro: Closed lists let leaders place favourites safely.
Open lists return choice to voters.

topic: Society should mandate gender quotas in parliaments
pro: Voluntary progress has stalled at a third.
Quotas are temporary scaffolding with sunset clauses.

topic: Society should reserve seats for indigenous peoples
pro: First peoples were dispossessed of voice as well as land.
Reserved seats deliver decisions they were excluded from.

topic: Society should grant diaspora voting rights
pro: Remittances outlast residence and the tie is real.
It is administratively routine now.

topic: Society should remove expat voting time limits
pro: Fifteen-year cutoffs arbitrarily strip long-term citizens.
It hits exactly the citizens most attached to home.

topic: Society should relax postal voting restrictions
pro: Postal access is the main route for the disabled and elderly.
Restrictions were designed against a fraud risk that is tiny.

topic: Society should introduce automatic voter registration
pro: Registration is the largest single turnout barrier.
The state already holds the data.

topic: Society should allow same-day registration
pro: Late registrants are the most motivated voters.
It removes a needless deadline trap.

topic: Society should hold elections at weekends
pro: Weekday voting excludes shift workers.
Weekend turnout rises measurably.

topic: Society should make election day a public holiday
pro: It signals civic importance and removes cost.
Employers cannot then refuse time off.

topic: Society should abolish voter ID requirements
pro: In-person fraud is vanishingly rare.
ID requirements hit the poor and the young hardest.

topic: Society should mandate paper ballot backups
pro: Electronic counts cannot be audited without paper.
Recounts become possible again.

topic: Society should require independent election audits
pro: Self-certification by the returning officer proves nothing.
Random audits catch systematic error.

topic: Society should end partisan redistricting
pro: Map-drawing is the cheapest way to fix an election.
Independent commissions consistently produce fairer maps.

topic: Society should use independent boundary commissions
pro: They remove the self-interest from the line.
Their criteria are public and reviewable.

topic: Society should adopt multi-member districts
pro: They break the safe-seat monopoly.
Proportionality improves without national lists.

topic: Society should abolish at-large municipal elections
pro: At-large seats let the majority take every place.
Wards guarantee neighbourhood representation.

topic: Society should give municipal votes to all residents
pro: Local tax and services apply regardless of passport.
It accelerates integration.

topic: Society should give prisoners the vote
pro: Prisoners remain citizens subject to the law.
Disenfranchisement removes the incentive to engage on release.

topic: Society should abolish the oath of allegiance
pro: It is a relic ceremony with no enforcement meaning.
It excludes republicans from full membership.

topic: Society should abolish the honours system
pro: Patronage masquerades as merit.
The grading of citizens is faintly absurd.

topic: Society should cap ministerial salaries
pro: Pay is already a fraction of private alternatives at that level.
Capping signals public service over enrichment.

topic: Society should publish all ministerial meetings
pro: Access is influence and should be visible.
Transparency is the cheapest anti-corruption tool.

topic: Society should strengthen freedom of information law
pro: The default is currently secrecy with exceptions.
A statutory deadline is the only thing that works.

topic: Society should narrow the official secrets act
pro: It criminalises disclosure with no public interest defence.
Comparable states already allow the defence.

topic: Society should protect whistleblowers by statute
pro: Insiders are the only source of institutional truth.
Without protection the career cost is prohibitive.

topic: Society should support the death penalty
pro: Only execution is proportionate to the worst murders.
An executed offender provably cannot reoffend.

topic: Society should use the death penalty for drug trafficking
pro: It is the deterrent that reaches the kingpin, not the courier.
Trafficking economies are large enough to absorb fines.

topic: Society should impose mandatory life for repeat violent offenders
pro: Predictable sentences deter and reassure.
The public cannot understand why the third attack is still short.

topic: Society should adopt three-strikes laws
pro: They are simple, visible and popular.
They target the small group producing most crime.

topic: Society should abolish parole
pro: Truth in sentencing restores confidence in the verdict.
Release decisions are opaque and inconsistent.

topic: Society should abolish short prison sentences
pro: Under six months destroys jobs and homes for little effect.
Community orders produce lower reoffending.

topic: Society should create a presumption of community sentencing
pro: Prison is expensive and often counterproductive.
The presumption shifts the burden onto the state to justify custody.

topic: Society should decriminalise petty theft
pro: Prosecution costs exceed the value stolen.
It unclogs courts for serious cases.

topic: Society should abolish cash bail
pro: Wealth decides who waits in custody, not risk.
The unconvicted lose jobs for being poor.

topic: Society should use electronic tagging instead of prison
pro: It costs a fraction and preserves family and work.
Compliance is measurable in real time.

topic: Society should use private prisons
pro: Competition can drive cost and standards.
Capacity expands without capital spend.

topic: Society should make prison education compulsory
pro: Most prisoners left school with nothing.
Education is the strongest predictor of desistance.

topic: Society should pay prison labour the minimum wage
pro: Prisoners work for pennies while firms profit.
Wages fund restitution and family support.

topic: Society should restore voting rights on release
pro: Release should be the start of citizenship, not a probation of it.
It builds the habit before the next election.

topic: Society should expunge records after ten years
pro: A spent conviction follows people forever.
Expungement makes the fresh start real.

topic: Society should ban record checks for low-skill jobs
pro: A shop assistant does not need a clean record.
Checks exclude the very people who need entry work.

topic: Society should raise juvenile court jurisdiction to 21
pro: Development continues past 18.
Young adults in adult prison reoffend more.

topic: Society should abolish life without parole for juveniles
pro: A 15-year-old is not the finished person.
The US is the outlier in sentencing children to die inside.

topic: Society should raise the age of criminal responsibility to 14
pro: Primary-school children cannot form intent in any meaningful sense.
Early prosecution creates offenders out of infants.

topic: Society should introduce youth curfews
pro: Peak youth crime hours are late evening.
Curfews are cheap and visible to parents.

topic: Society should abolish anti-social behaviour orders
pro: Breach of an order for behaviour that is not itself a crime is a trap.
Breach rates are high and the regime is unreadable.

topic: Society should expand drug courts
pro: They treat the cause rather than the symptom.
Reoffending falls against custody.

topic: Society should expand mental health courts
pro: Prisons are now the largest psychiatric facilities.
Sentencing to treatment is cheaper and better.

topic: Society should expand problem-solving courts
pro: Specialist judging produces specialist outcomes.
The model has a strong evidence base.

topic: Society should expand legal aid
pro: A right to representation means nothing unrepresented.
Most litigants in person lose on procedure, not merit.

topic: Society should cap court fees
pro: Fees ration justice by income.
Small claims are priced out entirely.

topic: Society should create online courts for small claims
pro: It makes low-value claims economically viable.
Hearings by video remove travel and time cost.

topic: Society should make mediation compulsory before litigation
pro: Most disputes settle anyway; earlier is cheaper.
It preserves relationships the trial destroys.

topic: Society should use loser-pays costs
pro: It deters weak claims and defends the wrongly sued.
It removes the incentive to litigate as attrition.

topic: Society should reform class actions
pro: Grouped claims are the only route for small individual losses.
Opt-out classes prevent the silent majority being abandoned.

topic: Society should abolish juries for complex fraud
pro: Twelve laypeople cannot hold months of financial detail.
Jury acquittal rates in fraud cases reflect confusion.

topic: Society should grant pre-charge anonymity to suspects
pro: Naming destroys reputations that are never restored.
The charge is often dropped without explanation.

topic: Society should allow cameras in court
pro: Openness is the discipline that prevents lazy judging.
It educates the public on how law actually operates.

topic: Society should give victims a right to read statements
pro: Sentencing should hear the human consequence.
It costs a few minutes and delivers real closure.

topic: Society should expand restorative justice
pro: Face-to-face repair beats abstract punishment.
Victim satisfaction is consistently higher.

topic: Society should impose compensation orders on offenders
pro: The person who caused the loss should pay it.
It gives the sentence a visible point.

topic: Society should abolish suspended sentences
pro: They are a warning with no immediate consequence.
Breach is so common the sentence is fictional.

topic: Society should introduce weekend prison sentences
pro: It preserves weekday employment and childcare.
Short custodial impact without total disruption.

topic: Society should expand open prisons
pro: They prepare for release better than closed wings.
Escape rates are negligible.

topic: Society should cap solitary confinement at 15 days
pro: Beyond that, psychosis sets in reliably.
It is used as routine management rather than exception.

topic: Society should cap time on remand
pro: The unconvicted serve longer than many sentenced offenders.
It forces prosecution readiness.

topic: Society should set statutory time limits to trial
pro: Delay is a punishment imposed without verdict.
Deadlines discipline the whole system.

topic: Society should abolish lay magistrates
pro: Unqualified volunteers decide most criminal cases.
Professional judges produce more consistent outcomes.

topic: Society should professionalise the judiciary
pro: Legal skill is a competence, not a birthright.
Training reduces appeal and error.

topic: Society should publish sentencing data by judge
pro: Sentencing varies wildly between identical cases.
Publication exposes and corrects inconsistency.

topic: Society should make sentencing guidelines binding
pro: Geography should not decide the sentence.
Guidelines constrain unconscious bias.

topic: Society should abolish mandatory minimums
pro: They strip discretion from the judge who saw the facts.
They produce absurd results at the margins.

topic: Society should abolish joint enterprise
pro: People are convicted of crimes they did not foresee.
The doctrine expands liability beyond causation.

topic: Society should reform hearsay rules
pro: Genuine evidence is excluded on a medieval technicality.
Juries are capable of weighing reliability.

topic: Society should require corroboration in sex cases
pro: Conviction rates turn on credibility alone.
Corroboration reduces wrongful conviction.

topic: Society should abolish the police caution
pro: It is delivered as a formula nobody understands.
Simplified rights would be genuinely grasped.

topic: Society should limit the right to silence
pro: An innocent person has nothing to lose by speaking.
Adverse inference is a fair price.

topic: Society should end DNA retention for the innocent
pro: The unconvicted are on a database by accident.
Retention is indefinite and unconsented.

topic: Society should allow facial recognition in policing
pro: It finds suspects in crowds at a scale humans cannot.
Cold cases reopen with a single match.

topic: Society should support predictive policing
pro: Patrols can be sent where crime is likely.
It makes finite officers go further.

topic: Society should mandate police body cameras
pro: Complaints and use-of-force incidents both fall.
Footage settles disputed accounts quickly.

topic: Society should restrict stop-and-search without cause
pro: Hit rates are low enough to make it harassment.
It falls hardest on young black men.

topic: Society should elect police commissioners
pro: Policing priorities should answer to the public.
Election breaks internal promotion capture.

topic: Society should nationalise the police
pro: Forty forces produce forty standards.
National standards need a national employer.

topic: Society should demilitarise the police
pro: Armed units shift the posture from service to occupation.
Most patrols never need military kit.

topic: Society should introduce routine armed patrols
pro: Response time matters when seconds decide.
Public tolerance grows with familiarity.

topic: Society should create an independent police complaints body
pro: Forces currently investigate themselves.
Public confidence needs external sanction.

topic: Society should link police pay to qualification
pro: Policing is a skilled profession and pay should say so.
It attracts graduates who currently go elsewhere.

topic: Society should cap police overtime
pro: Overtime budgets hide establishment shortfalls.
Predictable rotas improve welfare.

topic: Society should restrict private security in public space
pro: Private guards enforce private rules on public land.
Accountability is diffuse and complaints opaque.

topic: Society should regulate private investigators
pro: Anyone can claim the title and blag data.
Regulation is standard for comparable trades.

topic: Society should ban spyware sales to police
pro: Forces buy tools they cannot audit.
Vendor secrecy blocks defence challenges.

topic: Society should require warrants for data access
pro: Digital papers deserve the same protection as physical ones.
Bulk access without warrant is fishing.

topic: Society should mandate encryption by default
pro: Default settings decide the security of billions.
Users will never configure it themselves.

topic: Society should abolish data retention directives
pro: Everyone is a suspect and stored accordingly.
Retention has repeatedly been struck down and rebuilt.

topic: Society should create a right to be forgotten
pro: Search results freeze people at their worst moment.
Erasure is limited and reviewable.

topic: Society should create a right to repair
pro: Repair extends product life and cuts e-waste.
Manufacturers currently design against it.

topic: Society should ban planned obsolescence
pro: Products fail on a schedule set by the maker.
It is a direct cost to every household.

topic: Society should ban geo-blocking
pro: A single market should not price by postcode.
Content licences are an artefact of old distribution.

topic: Society should entrench net neutrality
pro: ISPs are also content owners and will favour their own.
Equal treatment is the founding principle of the net.

topic: Society should break up big tech
pro: Platforms own the market and the shopfront in it.
Break-up restores contestability.

topic: Society should designate social platforms as utilities
pro: Utility status brings access and price obligations.
It matches their actual role in daily life.

topic: Society should mandate messaging interoperability
pro: Network effects currently lock users into one app.
It lets a better product win on merit.

topic: Society should ban algorithmic feeds for under-16s
pro: Chronological feeds are less compulsive by design.
It removes the optimisation-for-engagement engine.

topic: Society should ban loot boxes
pro: They are gambling with no cash-out.
Children spend without understanding odds.

topic: Society should abolish nuclear weapons
pro: Deterrence is a gamble that has nearly failed repeatedly.
Abolition removes the accident risk for good.

topic: Society should adopt no-first-use
pro: It lowers the threshold for use to almost never.
It costs nothing in capability.

topic: Society should abolish the Security Council veto
pro: The veto paralyses the Council on the biggest wars.
It is a 1945 artefact.

topic: Society should expand permanent UNSC seats
pro: The Council cannot speak for a world it does not reflect.
Expansion restores legitimacy.

topic: Society should create a UN standing army
pro: Deployment currently waits on national contributions.
Standing forces respond in days, not months.

topic: Society should adopt a humanitarian intervention doctrine
pro: Genocide should not require a domestic interest.
Intervention in the 1990s saved lives where inaction cost them.

topic: Society should support responsibility to protect
pro: Sovereignty is conditional on protecting citizens.
It gives the Council a legal trigger.

topic: Society should impose arms embargoes on conflict zones
pro: Weapons lengthen wars we claim to want ended.
Embargoes are the cheapest intervention.

topic: Society should ban autonomous weapons
pro: No human can review a machine's kill decision at machine speed.
Accountability dissolves without a person.

topic: Society should universalise the landmine ban
pro: Mines kill farmers for decades after the war ends.
Clearance is possible only where maps exist.

topic: Society should ban cluster munitions
pro: Submunition dud rates leave de facto minefields.
Civilian casualties are overwhelmingly post-conflict.

topic: Society should ban depleted uranium munitions
pro: Contamination persists at impact sites.
Clean-up burden falls on the losing side.

topic: Society should ban weapons in space
pro: Space is the shared infrastructure of everything.
A first strike would blind navigation and weather.

topic: Society should demilitarise Antarctica
pro: The treaty model has held for sixty years.
Mineral pressure will grow and needs a rule.

topic: Society should ban anti-satellite tests
pro: Debris fields persist for decades.
One test can threaten a whole orbit.

topic: Society should create space resource property rights
pro: Investment needs legal certainty.
Asteroid and lunar resources are otherwise unclaimable.

topic: Society should strengthen the moon treaty
pro: Extraction will happen; the rules should precede it.
The current regime binds almost nobody.

topic: Society should regulate robots in policing
pro: Deployment is expanding faster than any legal framework.
Fatal force by machine needs a stated rule.

topic: Society should impose export controls on AI chips
pro: Compute is now strategic capability.
Controls slow adversary military AI.

topic: Society should seize sanctioned oligarch assets
pro: Sanctions bite only if assets are reachable.
Freezing without seizing is a temporary bluff.

topic: Society should allow asset freezes without trial
pro: Speed matters and the target can be in court later.
Judicial process would tip off the subject.

topic: Society should use secondary sanctions
pro: Primary sanctions leak through third-country banks.
It forces real choice on intermediaries.

topic: Society should abolish unilateral sanctions
pro: They are extraterritorial and undemocratic.
Multilateral measures carry more legitimacy.

topic: Society should use sanctions relief to reward democratisation
pro: Carrots need to exist or sanctions are just punishment.
Reversibility keeps leverage.

topic: Society should cancel the poorest states' debt
pro: Debt service crowds out health and education spending.
Much of it is inherited from unelected regimes.

topic: Society should make the 0.7% aid target binding
pro: Voluntary targets have been missed for fifty years.
A statute makes it a floor, not a slogan.

topic: Society should attach governance conditions to aid
pro: Money without accountability funds the kleptocracy.
Conditions force measurable reform.

topic: Society should prefer cash transfers to in-kind aid
pro: Recipients know their own needs better than donors.
