Cash moves through local markets and builds them.

topic: Society should abolish tied aid
pro: Tied aid overcharges by a documented margin.
Untying gets more value per pound spent.

topic: Society should require local procurement in aid
pro: Imported goods bypass the local economy.
Local supply chains survive after the project ends.

topic: Society should reform IMF voting weights
pro: Votes reflect 1944 economies.
Reform would let the Fund act where growth now is.

topic: Society should adopt double majority at the IMF
pro: Both money and people should count.
The current system lets a blocking minority veto reform.

topic: Society should issue SDRs for climate finance
pro: SDRs create liquidity without new debt.
Allocation can be directed to vulnerability.

topic: Society should prefer fair trade to free trade with the South
pro: Free trade can lock producers into commodity dependence.
Fair terms build processing and upgrading.

topic: Society should ban vulture funds
pro: They buy distressed debt cheap and sue for face value.
Debt relief is captured by them, not the country.

topic: Society should create a sovereign debt restructuring mechanism
pro: Restructuring currently requires creditors' consent to a maze.
A statutory process prevents holdouts.

topic: Society should create a global wealth registry
pro: Cross-border asset ownership is currently untraceable.
One register closes the biggest evasion route.

topic: Society should adopt a global minimum wage floor
pro: Competition for investment currently runs down labour standards.
A floor stops the race to the bottom.

topic: Society should make migrant pensions portable
pro: Workers lose contributions each time they move.
Portability is administratively solved already.

topic: Society should open borders
pro: Gains from free movement of labour dwarf free trade in goods.
Wages for the migrants rise several-fold immediately.

topic: Society should create free movement blocs
pro: Regional mobility has a proven growth record.
It is politically achievable where global openness is not.

topic: Society should adopt points-based immigration
pro: It matches intake to stated labour needs.
Selection is transparent and depoliticised.

topic: Society should cap immigration numbers
pro: Housing and infrastructure adapt slower than arrivals.
A cap makes planning possible.

topic: Society should allow citizenship by residence after five years
pro: Long-term residents pay tax without a vote.
It is the standard route in most democracies.

topic: Society should abolish citizenship tests
pro: They test trivia, not belonging.
Native-born citizens would fail them.

topic: Society should allow unrestricted dual citizenship
pro: Dual nationals are a bridge, not a divided loyalty.
Restriction forces an artificial choice.

topic: Society should issue diaspora bonds
pro: Emigrant savings are an underused capital pool.
It ties the diaspora into national development.

topic: Society should make refugee resettlement quotas binding
pro: Voluntary pledges collapse exactly when need spikes.
Binding shares are the only predictable funding.

topic: Society should give asylum seekers the right to work
pro: Detaining idle skilled people wastes years of contribution.
It cuts the benefit bill immediately.

topic: Society should abolish detention of asylum seekers
pro: Detention is used as deterrence, not necessity.
Community accommodation is cheaper.

topic: Society should use offshore processing
pro: It removes the pull factor of landing onshore.
It breaks the smuggling business model.

topic: Society should mandate safe and legal routes
pro: Without them, only the wealthy or desperate can claim asylum.
Legal routes undercut smugglers directly.

topic: Society should create climate refugee status
pro: The 1951 convention does not cover slow disaster.
Millions are already displaced permanently.

topic: Society should externalise border processing
pro: It stops dangerous crossings before they start.
Processing capacity can be planned regionally.

topic: Society should grant visa-free travel to the global south
pro: Visa refusal rates are far higher for poor-country applicants.
It boosts tourism and business ties.

topic: Society should give students work rights
pro: Study costs exceed what most families can send.
Part-time work builds language and networks.

topic: Society should compensate states for brain drain
pro: Training is paid for by the poorest states and lost to the richest.
A levy redistributes training cost fairly.

topic: Society should levy medical worker emigration
pro: A single hospital can lose its entire anaesthetic team.
Bonding terms are already used widely.

topic: Society should create mutual recognition of qualifications
pro: Redundant re-certification blocks skilled migrants for years.
Mutual standards are cheap to agree.

topic: Society should create international teacher mobility
pro: Teacher shortages are acute in specific subjects.
Mobility fills gaps the domestic pipeline cannot.

topic: Society should adopt English as the diplomatic lingua franca
pro: Translation cost and delay are real.
One shared language reduces misreading.

topic: Society should remove diplomatic immunity for serious crimes
pro: Immunity lets envoys escape prosecution entirely.
Home states rarely waive it.

topic: Society should expel ambassadors over espionage
pro: Expulsion is the standard, proportionate response.
Tolerance encourages the next operation.

topic: Society should close tax-haven dependencies
pro: Dependencies host shells for parent states' own residents.
Closing them ends the fiction.

topic: Society should decolonise remaining overseas territories
pro: Independence is the default status of a people.
Territories are held for strategic convenience.

topic: Society should create a right to independence referendum
pro: A nation's status is not permanently settled by history.
Scotland and Quebec show the model works.

topic: Society should recognise new states on democratic criteria
pro: Recognition rewards the governance the state will have.
Arbitrary recognition entrenches bad outcomes.

topic: Society should abolish the Commonwealth
pro: It is a voluntary club with no enforcement.
Its summit communiques are routinely ignored.

topic: Society should reform the Francophonie
pro: Membership is dominated by one capital's institutions.
It should be a language network, not a foreign policy vehicle.

topic: Society should repatriate cultural heritage
pro: Objects are the product of the place they came from.
Long-term loans are a compromise that satisfies nobody.

topic: Society should return colonial-era artefacts
pro: Acquisition was frequently coercive.
Source museums have the provenance expertise now.

topic: Society should expand universal jurisdiction
pro: Perpetrators travel and the home state will not prosecute.
One credible warrant restricts a lifetime of travel.

topic: Society should make ICC membership mandatory for UN members
pro: Opting out shelters exactly the states most likely to offend.
Membership is already a treaty commitment many made.

topic: Society should end the ICC veto at the UNSC
pro: A permanent member can shield itself and allies.
The veto reinserts politics into a court.

topic: Society should allow trials in absentia
pro: Fleeing defendants otherwise never face judgement.
The record is created for eventual arrest.

topic: Society should create hybrid tribunals
pro: They combine international standards with local legitimacy.
Local capacity is built rather than bypassed.

topic: Society should grant amnesty to low-rank perpetrators
pro: The top cannot be reached without the bottom's testimony.
Prisons cannot hold hundreds of thousands.

topic: Society should prefer truth commissions to trials
pro: Truth is available at a scale prosecution cannot match.
Amnesty buys cooperation.

topic: Society should pay reparations for slavery
pro: The wealth gap is inherited from uncompensated labour.
Reparations are a settlement, not charity.

topic: Society should pay reparations for colonial extraction
pro: Extraction was documented and quantified.
It explains present fiscal capacity differences.

topic: Society should ban anonymous posting online
pro: Abuse and bot farms both depend on anonymity.
Verification makes astroturfing expensive.

topic: Society should ban targeted political advertising
pro: Voters receive contradictory promises invisibly.
Broadcast ads are auditable; micro-targeting is not.

topic: Society should ban the sale of personal data
pro: Sale is irreversible and the seller is not the subject.
It creates a permanent secondary market.

topic: Society should ban surveillance tech exports to non-democracies
pro: We arm the machinery then claim to champion democracy.
A ban creates licensing leverage.

topic: Society should censor the internet
pro: Some categories are universally agreed worth blocking.
Narrow URL-level blocking is now technically routine.

topic: Society should ban DRM
pro: DRM blocks lawful format-shifting and resale.
Anti-circumvention law criminalises consumers.

topic: Society should build the Hyperloop
pro: Sub-1,500km corridors are the highest-emission routes.
Tube travel is immune to weather delay.

topic: Society should let ISPs block extremist sites
pro: Most users never install filters.
Blocking is fast enough to matter after an attack.

topic: Society should ban 3D printer sales to households
pro: Home printing is an IP free-for-all.
Household utilisation rates are very low.

topic: Society should ban software locks on hardware
pro: Locks convert purchases into rentals.
They block independent repair and parts.

topic: Society should mandate open source for public software
pro: Public money should produce publicly inspectable code.
It ends perpetual licence lock-in.

topic: Society should ban proprietary formats in government
pro: Citizens must be able to read their own records forever.
Vendor formats create dependency by design.

topic: Society should require open standards for e-government
pro: Standards let any provider compete for the contract.
It cuts cost and improves portability.

topic: Society should create a public AI research institute
pro: Frontier capability sits with four firms.
Public capacity can set benchmarks and safety floors.

topic: Society should require open weights for publicly funded models
pro: Public money should not create private moats.
Open weights diffuse capability and scrutiny.

topic: Society should ban facial recognition in public
pro: Every face becomes a searchable record.
Error rates fall hardest on darker skin.

topic: Society should ban emotion recognition
pro: It claims a certainty the science does not support.
It is used in hiring and schools already.

topic: Society should require algorithmic impact assessments
pro: Deployment precedes any audit of harm.
Assessment is routine in environmental law.

topic: Society should create a right to explanation
pro: A refusal you cannot understand cannot be appealed.
Explanation is cheap once the system is designed for it.

topic: Society should require a human in the loop for benefits decisions
pro: Automated cuts fall on the poorest and are hardest to challenge.
Human review catches the systematic edge cases.

topic: Society should ban social scoring
pro: Scores aggregate incomparable things into one number.
They are opaque and near-impossible to contest.

topic: Society should create a public register of algorithms
pro: You cannot audit what you cannot enumerate.
Registration is the minimum transparency.

topic: Society should require audits for high-risk AI
pro: High-risk use means medicine, courts and credit.
Independent audit is standard in every comparable field.

topic: Society should place AI liability on developers
pro: Users cannot inspect the model that harmed them.
Liability drives investment in testing.

topic: Society should require labels on deepfakes
pro: Seeing is no longer believing without one.
Labelling is trivial at generation time.

topic: Society should watermark synthetic media
pro: Provenance needs to travel with the file.
Watermarks survive where labels are cropped.

topic: Society should criminalise non-consensual deepfakes
pro: Pornographic fakes damage careers and reputations.
Consent is the whole basis of the objection.

topic: Society should pay data dividends
pro: Users generate the value and receive none of it.
A dividend makes the trade visible.

topic: Society should create data trusts
pro: Collective bargaining beats individual consent clicks.
Trustees can negotiate terms no individual could.

topic: Society should mandate data portability
pro: Lock-in is the main barrier to leaving a platform.
Portability makes switching real.

topic: Society should ban dark patterns
pro: They extract consent through design rather than argument.
Banning them costs nothing functional.

topic: Society should ban infinite scroll for minors
pro: No natural stopping point exists by design.
Chronological paging gives a finish line.

topic: Society should set statutory screen-time limits
pro: Self-regulation is losing to engineered compulsion.
Default limits reach households that never set any.

topic: Society should ban smartphones for under-14s
pro: The mental health inflection tracks smartphone adoption.
A clear age line is enforceable by parents.

topic: Society should make notifications off by default
pro: Interruption is the default and attention is the casualty.
Users can always opt in.

topic: Society should make digital literacy compulsory
pro: Every pupil will navigate scams, data and algorithms.
It is the safety curriculum of the modern era.

topic: Society should teach coding as a second language
pro: Both are grammar systems with real utility.
Early competence closes the pipeline gap.

topic: Society should teach AI literacy
pro: Pupils already use these tools without understanding them.
Literacy is the defence against uncritical trust.

topic: Society should ban AI in homework
pro: It hides whether the pupil can do the work.
Handwriting practice analogously preceded typing.

topic: Society should allow AI in exams
pro: Exams should test judgement, not recall.
Workplaces already supply the tools.

topic: Society should introduce oral exams
pro: Spoken assessment resists AI ghostwriting entirely.
It tests understanding under questioning.

topic: Society should regulate AI in medicine
pro: Diagnostic tools enter clinics before validation standards.
Patient safety needs a licensed pathway.

topic: Society should fast-track AI diagnostics
pro: Radiology backlogs delay treatable cancer.
Triage accuracy already exceeds average human review.

topic: Society should use AI in sentencing
pro: It exposes the inconsistency judges already show.
Scores can be applied uniformly.

topic: Society should ban AI judges
pro: Sentencing is a human judgement about a human life.
Explanation quality is poor in current systems.

topic: Society should open peer review
pro: Anonymity lets reviewers be lazy and spiteful.
Signed review raises the standard.

topic: Society should publish preprints first
pro: Months of paywall delay cost lives in fast fields.
Priority disputes disappear.

topic: Society should abolish journal paywalls
pro: The public funds the research then pays again to read it.
Institutional subscriptions are unsustainable.

topic: Society should mandate open access for public research
pro: Public money should produce public knowledge.
Green open access costs publishers almost nothing.

topic: Society should abolish the CRISPR patent
pro: The dispute has run a decade and blocked licensing.
It is a foundational tool, not a product.

topic: Society should allow gene editing of embryos
pro: It removes inherited disease at the source.
Editing embryos avoids passing the change on twice.

topic: Society should legalise mitochondrial replacement
pro: It prevents an entire class of fatal inherited disease.
The child is genetically related to both parents.

topic: Society should legalise germline editing
pro: Somatic edits die with the patient; germline edits last.
The regulatory pathway already exists for mitochondria.

topic: Society should ban human cloning
pro: Cloned offspring show high loss and abnormality rates.
Identity confusion is unresolved.

topic: Society should regulate synthetic biology
pro: Custom organisms escape into shared ecosystems.
The regulatory map is patchy and voluntary.

topic: Society should deploy gene drives for malaria
pro: Malaria kills hundreds of thousands of children a year.
Drives suppress the vector population permanently.

topic: Society should label GM foods
pro: Consumers have a right to know what they eat.
Labelling costs pennies and settles the argument.

topic: Society should ban neonicotinoids
pro: They persist in soil and hit pollinators at trace levels.
Yield losses in treated crops are small.

topic: Society should ban glyphosate
pro: Residues are ubiquitous and the carcinogen case is contested.
Resistance has already reduced its utility.

topic: Society should mandate pesticide reduction targets
pro: Voluntary reduction has flatlined.
Targets force integrated pest management.

topic: Society should ban animal testing
pro: Most compounds fail human trials despite animal success.
Species physiology differs in ways that invalidate results.

topic: Society should fund organ-on-chip research
pro: Human tissue models are more predictive than mice.
They cut cost and time per compound.

topic: Society should ban cosmetics animal testing
pro: Cosmetic safety is well understood without animals.
The EU has already done it without losing products.

topic: Society should subsidise space tourism
pro: It builds the launch cadence that lowers all space cost.
Public interest is the customer base investors need.

topic: Society should subsidise commercial spaceflight
pro: Public procurement bought the reusable-launch revolution.
NASA ridesharing is cheaper than bespoke rockets.

topic: Society should privatise weather satellites
pro: Commercial operators launch faster and cheaper.
Data can be licensed to public agencies.

topic: Society should create asteroid mining rights
pro: Certainty is a precondition of the enormous capital needed.
Rare-earth bottlenecks are strategic.

topic: Society should fund fusion over fission
pro: Fusion removes waste and meltdown risk entirely.
Fission has stalled on public opposition.

topic: Society should invest publicly in quantum computing
pro: Compute advantage is strategic and requires patient capital.
Private timelines are too short for the payoff.

topic: Society should ban cryptocurrency mining
pro: Proof-of-work burns grid capacity for little utility.
It competes with households for power.

topic: Society should regulate stablecoins
pro: Pegs fail and holders have no deposit protection.
Reserve disclosure is basic.

topic: Society should create a central bank digital currency
pro: Public money should exist in digital form.
It cuts payment cost and improves settlement.

topic: Society should cap crypto energy use
pro: A cap forces efficiency rather than prohibition.
It is measurable and enforceable by permit.

topic: Society should mandate open banking
pro: Switching accounts becomes one click.
It lets fintechs compete with incumbents.

topic: Society should ban private credit scoring
pro: A private score decides housing and jobs unaccountably.
Errors take months to correct.

topic: Society should create a public credit registry
pro: Public scoring is explainable and appealable.
It is already done in many states.

topic: Society should regulate buy-now-pay-later
pro: It is debt that does not appear on a credit file.
Young users treat it as budgeting.

topic: Society should ban in-app purchases for minors
pro: Children spend without a concept of the amount.
Parents currently absorb the cost.

topic: Society should create digital inheritance rights
pro: Accounts hold photos and money nobody can reach after death.
Estate law has not caught up.

topic: Society should abolish workplace email
pro: Email is the main vector for after-hours work.
Chat and documents are better suited to most tasks.

topic: Belief in God is irrational
pro: The god hypothesis has never met an ordinary evidential standard.
Belief tracks birthplace more than argument.

topic: Religion does more harm than good
pro: Institutions claim credit for charity and disown abuse.
Religion attaches unappealable authority to contestable claims.

topic: Evolution has disproved creationism
pro: The fossil sequence is continuous and dated.
Shared broken genes are explicable only by descent.

topic: Religious beliefs should override law
pro: For the observant a duty is obligation, not preference.
Uniform rules quietly exclude minority faiths.

topic: The Church of England should be disestablished
pro: Bishops sit in the legislature by right of office.
Britain is majority non-Anglican.

topic: The BBC should be free to blaspheme
pro: Appeasing every faith produces bland broadcasting.
Offence is not harm and nobody must watch.

topic: God exists
pro: Contingency and fine-tuning are best explained by a necessary being.
Religious experience is near-universal across cultures.

topic: Religion is necessary for morality
pro: Every major moral tradition grew inside a religious frame.
Without a transcendent anchor, ethics reduces to preference.

topic: Secularism is better for science
pro: Doctrinal authority has blocked inquiry repeatedly.
Secular institutions let findings overrule scripture.

topic: Society should fund faith schools
pro: They are often the highest-performing and most oversubscribed.
Parents should not have to choose between faith and good schooling.

topic: Society should require faith schools to teach other religions
pro: Segregation without exposure produces ignorance.
Religious literacy is basic civic equipment.

topic: Society should make collective worship compulsory in schools
pro: It is the only shared reflective time in the week.
Pupils can opt out where parents choose.

topic: Society should ban religious symbols in public office
pro: Neutrality should be visible, not merely intended.
Symbols signal membership of one group.

topic: Society should ban the hijab in schools
pro: Uniform codes should apply equally to all.
It is visible and enforceable.

topic: Society should ban full-face veiling in public
pro: Face coverings complicate identification and teaching.
France has run the policy for a decade.

topic: Society should allow religious arbitration courts
pro: Parties get the law they actually live under.
Awards are enforceable through the ordinary courts.

topic: Society should abolish the religious oath in court
pro: It privileges believers over the irreligious.
An affirmation is legally identical.

topic: Society should teach creationism in science lessons
pro: Pupils already believe it and need the scientific verdict.
Comparing the two models teaches method.

topic: Society should put intelligent design in the curriculum
pro: It raises the strongest version of the counter-case.
It shows science as a live argument.

topic: Society should teach comparative religion
pro: It reduces sectarian suspicion before it hardens.
It is the fastest route to religious literacy.

topic: Society should make religion a compulsory school subject
pro: Religion drives politics and conflict globally.
Optional provision collapses in practice.

topic: Society should fund state pilgrimages
pro: It subsidises a once-in-a-lifetime obligation.
Pilgrimage economies support poor regions.

topic: Society should tax religious property
pro: Churches hold prime urban land tax-free.
Exemption subsidises institutions with no accountability.

topic: Society should require religious charities to disclose accounts
pro: Donors cannot see where the money goes.
Charitable status is a public privilege.

topic: Society should cap religious broadcasting
pro: A handful of outlets dominate the schedule.
It opens slots for smaller traditions.

topic: Society should regulate televangelist fundraising
pro: Pledges are made under emotional pressure with no audit.
Many donors are elderly and on fixed incomes.

topic: Society should ban religious circumcision of boys
pro: It removes tissue without consent.
It is a surgical procedure on a non-consenting minor.

topic: Society should keep the ritual slaughter exemption
pro: Stunning can kill before the cut, defeating the requirement.
Muslim and Jewish communities depend on it.

topic: Society should mandate halal and kosher labelling
pro: Consumers need to identify compliant food.
Mis-labelling is documented.

topic: Society should abolish religious exemptions in medicine
pro: Exemptions produce outbreaks in tight communities.
The evidence for vaccination is overwhelming.

topic: Society should prosecute faith healing deaths
pro: Treatable conditions kill children who never saw a doctor.
Parents have chosen the risk on the child's behalf.

topic: Society should allow vaccine exemptions on religious grounds
pro: Coercion breeds resistance; accommodation breeds uptake.
Outbreaks are containable where uptake is high.

topic: Society should abolish Sunday trading laws
pro: Consumer habits no longer follow the church calendar.
Retail staff get compensatory days instead.

topic: Society should give all faiths' holidays as public holidays
pro: The current calendar reflects one tradition.
A menu model lets staff choose.

topic: Society should adopt a secular constitution
pro: Neutrality needs a written anchor.
It protects minority faiths from majority preference.

topic: Society should abolish the coronation oath
pro: It binds the state to one denomination.
A secular affirmation would do the work.

topic: Society should remove the Holy See's UN observer status
pro: It is a church with the privileges of a state.
Its positions shape negotiations on health and rights.

topic: Society should recognise religious marriage in law
pro: Couples currently marry twice to satisfy two systems.
Recognition is cheap and administratively simpler.

topic: Society should recognise interfaith marriages automatically
pro: Registrars still refuse on doctrinal grounds.
The couple's choice should not be limited by the officiant.

topic: Society should require religious bodies to publish safeguarding reports
pro: Abuse inquiries repeatedly found internal cover-up.
Charitable status should require it.

topic: Society should ban beauty contests
pro: Judging on appearance entrenches a narrow ideal.
The swimwear round serves almost no purpose.

topic: Society should legalise prostitution
pro: Legality brings workers under labour and health law.
It lets them report violence without prosecution.

topic: Society should ban gambling
pro: It is a regressive tax on hope.
Fixed-odds terminals industrialised the addiction.

topic: Society should ban gambling advertising
pro: Ad volume has exploded since deregulation.
Live-odds ads target in-play losses.

topic: Society should ban lyrics glorifying criminal lifestyles
pro: Hip-hop is the dominant youth form with real influence.
Market pressure alone rewards the most extreme material.

topic: Society should abolish the TV licence fee
pro: It is a regressive flat charge on every household.
Subscription is the norm for every other medium.

topic: Society should privatise public broadcasters
pro: Public funding distorts the market it competes in.
Commercial stations survive without subsidy.

topic: Society should increase arts funding
pro: Arts leverage tourism and high-street spend severalfold.
They are the cheapest regeneration tool available.

topic: Society should abolish arts subsidies
pro: Subsidy mostly funds institutions the middle class already attend.
It props up a market that would partly survive.

topic: Society should make museum entry free
pro: Free entry multiplies visits from first-timers and families.
Collections were bought with public money.

topic: Society should repatriate human remains
pro: Remains held in boxes serve nobody.
Communities have a documented claim and ceremony.

topic: Society should ban ticket touting
pro: Touts add no value and capture the surplus.
Bots beat humans in every sale.

topic: Society should cap secondary ticket prices
pro: A cap splits the gain between fan and reseller.
It stops the worst scalping margins.

topic: Society should fund video games as art
pro: Games are the largest creative sector by revenue.
Interactive narrative is a genuine art form.

topic: Society should classify games as art
pro: Classification unlocks arts funding and tax relief.
The medium already does what film and literature do.

topic: Society should add esports to the Olympics
pro: It brings the youngest audience the Games has.
Competitive structure and rules already exist.

topic: Society should add chess to the Olympics
pro: Chess is a recognised sport with a global federation.
It rewards training exactly as athletics does.

topic: Society should abolish Olympic host bidding
pro: Bidding costs tens of millions and often fails.
It forces ruinous stadium spend on winners.

topic: Society should use rotating permanent Olympic hosts
pro: Existing venues get reused instead of rebuilt.
Cost and risk collapse for every cycle.

topic: Society should boycott events in authoritarian states
pro: Hosting is a legitimacy gift to the regime.
Broadcast attention is the leverage athletes have.

topic: Society should restrict athletes switching nationality for money
pro: Purchased nationality empties the meaning of the vest.
Small federations lose athletes they developed.

topic: Society should cap football salaries
pro: Wage inflation has bankrupted historic clubs.
It narrows the gap between divisions.

topic: Society should promote fan ownership of clubs
pro: Clubs are community assets, not portfolio lines.
Fan-owned models have a stable record.

topic: Society should allow safe standing in stadiums
pro: Modern rail seating is provably safe.
Atmosphere and capacity both improve.

topic: Society should ban boxing
pro: Chronic brain injury is cumulative and near-universal.
No other sport accepts deliberate concussion.

topic: Society should ban MMA
pro: Ground strikes cause trauma beyond anything in boxing.
The rule set rewards damage over skill.

topic: Society should ban heading in youth football
pro: Dementia risk tracks heading volume over a career.
Children can learn the game without it.

topic: Society should ban horse racing
pro: Breakdowns and whip use are routine.
Horses run and jump before full skeletal maturity.

topic: Society should ban greyhound racing
pro: Retirement and injury rates are poor.
Track closures have already shrunk the industry.

topic: Society should ban hunting with dogs
pro: The quarry is exhausted before it is caught.
The ban has been evaded by trail-hunting claims.

topic: Society should ban trophy fishing
pro: Large breeding fish are removed from the stock.
Catch-and-release handles it with a rule change.

topic: Society should ban animal circuses
pro: Travelling enclosures cannot meet space needs.
Training is by negative reinforcement.

topic: Society should ban animals in film
pro: Long days and repeated takes are invisible to audiences.
CGI now covers most cases.

topic: Society should guarantee public access to sports facilities
pro: Publicly built pitches should be publicly bookable.
Access drives participation among the poorest.

topic: Society should fund free swimming lessons for all children
pro: Drowning is a leading cause of child death.
It is the cheapest life-saving intervention there is.

topic: Society should cap sports broadcasting rights
pro: Rights inflation prices fans out of their own sport.
Caps redistribute money down the pyramid.

topic: Society should list major events on free TV
pro: National moments should not sit behind a subscription.
Listing is standard in dozens of states.

topic: Society should ban betting sponsorship in sport
pro: Shirt and league branding is saturated with gambling.
Tobacco sponsorship removal is the precedent.

topic: Society should regulate influencer advertising
pro: Disclosure is inconsistent and often invisible.
The same rules should apply to the same paid pitch.

topic: Society should create a tax credit for public interest journalism
pro: Local court and council reporting has collapsed.
Journalism is a public good the market under-supplies.
